semantics: rust-rrule (a Rust port of python-dateutil's rrule). Two test styles are converted: (1) string tests (rfc_tests.rs, regression.rs, daylight_saving.rs): "DTSTART...\nRRULE...".parse::<RRuleSet>() then .all(N) (at most N instances; u16::MAX = effectively all) or .all_unchecked(), compared with common::check_occurrences(&dates, &[RFC 3339 strings]); the RFC 3339 values are converted to wall-clock basic form in the DTSTART zone (tzid) - the UTC offsets in the source are consistent with that zone. (2) struct tests (rrule.rs): RRule { freq, count, interval, until, week_start, by_* .. } + test_recurring_rrule(rrule, limited, dt_start, &[expected]) where dt_start/expected are ymd_hms(...) in UTC (written with a Z suffix); the struct fields were mapped to RRULE text (by_n_month_day merged into BYMONTHDAY; NWeekday::Nth(n, D) -> nDD); the explicit by_hour/by_minute/by_second/by_month/by_month_day values that the tests copy from dt_start are kept verbatim. As in dateutil, DTSTART is NOT emitted unless it matches the rule (include_dtstart=false). 'limit' = N for .all(N) with N != u16::MAX. Tests gated by #[cfg(feature = "by-easter")] carry extensions ["BYEASTER"]. Tests that build rules with the builder API, use RRuleSet builders (rruleset.rs), assert something other than the instance list, or are not mechanically extractable were skipped.
